verdict: Nike closed its fiscal year with revenue down 2% to $12.6B, but a wider gross margin and lower overhead lifted net income 45% to $1.5B.

segments.name: North America
segments.note: Nike's home market — footwear fell 6%, apparel rose 4%, and equipment jumped 47%.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: Nike's second-biggest region — footwear fell 5%, apparel rose 1%, equipment rose 28%.

segments.name: Asia Pacific & Latin America
segments.note: Footwear was flat, apparel rose 2% and equipment rose 11%.

segments.name: Converse
segments.note: The Chuck Taylor brand — revenue fell 18% on declines in North America and Western Europe.

segments.name: Global Brand & Corporate
segments.note: Global Brand Divisions revenue of $11M plus Corporate of -$23M, mostly currency-hedge results — a small negative this quarter.

opex.name: Demand creation
opex.note: Advertising and brand marketing — lower sports marketing expense was offset by higher advertising and marketing expense.

opex.name: Operating overhead
opex.note: Running the company — wages, distribution centers and administration — including $39M of restructuring charges.

otherDetail: $53M of net interest income, plus $127M of other income, net.
footerNote: Segment revenues are Nike's divisional revenues; 'Global Brand & Corporate' combines Global Brand Divisions ($11M) and Corporate (-$23M, mostly currency-hedge results) — a small negative this quarter.

takeaways.title: Revenue slipped at the finish
takeaways.text: Revenue fell 2% to $12,606M: North America eased 1% and Converse dropped 18%, partly offset by Greater China up 3% and Asia Pacific & Latin America up 1%. Full-year revenue was $51.4B, roughly flat.

takeaways.title: Margin widened anyway
takeaways.text: Gross margin rose 110 basis points to 44.7% on strategic pricing and lower ocean freight and logistics costs, and operating overhead fell 9% on lower wage-related expenses — so profit grew even as sales shrank.

takeaways.title: Profit jumped against a weak comparison
takeaways.text: Net income rose 45% to $1,500M and EPS to $0.99, against a year-ago quarter weighed down by a higher tax rate and weaker margins. EPS included $0.02 of restructuring charges; excluding them it would have been $1.01.

oneTimers: Operating overhead includes $39M of restructuring charges as Nike streamlined the organization ($0.02 per share, net of tax benefit). Excluding these charges, diluted EPS would have been $1.01.
